messages:
Alex: quick summary of the positional-embedding scaling sweep I ran this morning (llama/mistral/mixtral/qwen) — trying linear vs NTK vs YARN variants, and also testing kernel selection + batching impacts. TL;DR: some surprising perf/quality tradeoffs, see below.
Maria: awesome — can you paste the profiler output and the exact config flags you used?
Alex: pasted minimal configs and perf snippets: 
```
models: [llama-13b, mixtral-8x7b, qwen-7b, mistral-7b]
rope_variant: [linear, ntk, yarn]
rope_scale: [0.8, 1.0, 1.2]
batch_policy: [static(8), dynamic(64ms), auto_prefetch]
kernel_policy: prefer_triton_if_available=true
kv_policy: prefix_cache_enabled=true, max_prefetch_tokens=1024
```
Alex: profiler links: flamegraphs in CI -> https://ci.internal/runs/17950/flame (private) ; summary below.
Maria: nice. quick notes from the traces: when we force Triton kernels for mixed-attn on mixtral, we get ~12-18% throughput uplift for short sequences (<512) but tail latency increases for long ctx because Triton's fused kernels aren't as memory-friendly for KV growth.
Samir: did you see any memory spikes tied to kv cache layout (heads vs kv_dim ordering)? we had previously seen allocator churn when kv is kept head-major.
Alex: yes — on Mistral variants, the NTK rope + scale=1.2 case caused KV buffer allocations to jump ~30% at 8k context. That triggered more frequent GC and host->device remapping. On Mixtral we saw a correctness-ish signal: perplexity on long-context evals increased ~0.6 ppl for NTK vs linear; quality looked fine under 2k.
Jin: from the perf counters I inspected: kernel selection switched from cuBLAS matmul -> Triton grouped-bmm at token 256 boundary. The decision came from our kernel-selector heuristics (seq_len * batch > 131072). That threshold might be too low for models with large head dims (mixtral heads=64).
Maria: that threshold was tuned on Llama-ish dims. For mixtral and qwen, the head_kv_dim is different so the token*batch heuristic isn't a perfect proxy. We should add a head_kv_dim factor to the decision rule.
Samir: proposal: change selection rule to: choose_triton if (seq_len * batch * (head_kv_dim/64) < threshold_adj). Essentially scale the threshold by head_kv_dim/64. Quick A/B could validate.
Alex: I ran that locally — scaling threshold by head_kv_dim reduced the long-ctx latency spikes and kept throughput wins for short ctx. But two caveats: 1) NTK variant still shows the perplexity bump on mixtral at >4k, 2) KV cache memory footprint remains larger than linear rope for some configurations.
Jin: can you paste the profiling snippet (timing per op) you mentioned?
Alex: pasted a short excerpt: 
```
Mixtral-ntk-scale1.2, seq=8192, batch=1:
  attn_forward_triton: 82ms
  kv_write: 48ms (host memcpy spikes)
  backend_alloc: 120ms (realloc)
  total: 260ms
Mixtral-linear-scale1.0, seq=8192, batch=1:
  attn_forward_cublas: 110ms
  kv_write: 32ms
  backend_alloc: 45ms
  total: 190ms
```
Maria: backend_alloc being so high indicates allocator churn — likely because we grow kv buffers per-request under the NTK implementation. We should pre-reserve based on max_prefetch_tokens and reuse across requests.
Samir: on batching heuristics: dynamic batching at 64ms gives better average latency for web workloads but amplifies KV cache pressure because more concurrent sequences mean more concurrent KV allocations. For Private/Dedicated customers we can recommend static(8) or auto_prefetch that pre-allocates.
Alex: agree. action items I propose: 1) tweak kernel selector to include head_kv_dim factor (Samir to PR), 2) add pre-reserve path for KV buffers when prefix_cache_enabled (Maria to prototype), 3) longer evals for NTK on mixtral & qwen to measure quality regression surface (Jin to run), 4) add a perf CI job that runs seq=4k/8k trials nightly for each model/rope-variant (perf-bot to schedule).
perf-bot: scheduled nightly-ropesweep-longctx job -> run_id=nightly-17950, will post results to #eng-runtime after completion :robot_face: 
Jin: one more datapoint — YARN variant behaved like a middle ground: throughput close to linear for long ctx but some numeric drift on attention accumulation for qwen at scale>6k. Might be worth flagging YARN as "safe for up to 6k" per-model.
Maria: agreed. We should publish a per-model safe-range table in the runtime docs showing recommended rope_variant and max_context. I'll draft it after we get Jin's evals.
Samir: FYI I ran a quick end-to-end latency smoke with the head_kv_dim threshold tweak and saw 8% p95 improvement for Mixtral at seq=2k and no throughput regression at seq=128. Will open PR with perf numbers.
Alex: great. I'll collate the logs and add attachments to the issue. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks — ping me when PRs are ready and I'll run the preflight jobs.
Jin: filing eval runs now, will post summary tomorrow.
Alex: closing loop: we should avoid automatic NTK for mixtral/qwen until we have long-ctx quality signoff. For now recommend linear or YARN with per-model max_context constraints.
Maria: notes captured in the runtime task: https://boards.internal/t/RT-846 (private).
